αἰθούσης: αἴθουσα — portico, colonnade; fem. gen. sg.
αἰπὺ: αἰπύς — steep, sheer; adj., neut. acc. sg., agreeing with ὄρος · also with other neut. nouns (αἰπὺ πτολίεθρον ’steep citadel’)

αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg.: ’himself’ · also masc. nom. sg. with a 1st-person subject: ’myself’ (ἐγὼν αὐτός) · also masc. nom. sg. with a 2nd-person subject: ’yourself’ (εἰδήσεις δὲ καὶ αὐτός ’you will see for yourself’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε

βροτοῖσιν: βροτός — mortal, mortal man; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οῖς)

γέροντι: γέρων — old man; masc. dat. sg.

γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γείνατο: γείνομαι — beget, bear (of a mother); aor. 3 sg. mid., epic, unaugmented (= ἐγείνατο)
γενεήν: γενεή — birth, race, lineage; acc. sg., Ionic η (= Attic γενεά)
γυναίων: γύναιος — of a woman, women’s; neut. gen. pl., poetic (= Attic γυναικείων), with δώρων: ’women’s gifts’ (the Greek does not say whether given to a woman or by one)
δεσμῷ: δεσμός — bond, fetter; masc. dat. sg.
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
διοκλῆος: Διοκλῆς — Diocles, host of Telemachus at Pherae; masc. gen. sg.
διοτρεφές: διοτρεφής — Zeus-nurtured (epithet of kings); adj., masc. voc. sg.

δύσετό: δύω/δύνω — sink, set (of the sun); aor. mid. 3 sg., unaugmented

δώρων: δῶρον — gift; neut. gen. pl., partitive with κειμήλια: ’of the gifts’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῆμον: δῆμος — people, land, community; masc. acc. sg.
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb: ’the house’

εἶχε: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., augmented (contracted from ἔ-εχε): ’held’

εὐχόμεθ: εὔχομαι — declare oneself, avow; pres. 1 pl., elided (εὐχόμεθ’ = εὐχόμεθα)

θοὴν: θοός — swift, quick; fem. acc. sg.
θοῇ: θοός — swift, quick (standing epithet of ships); fem. dat. sg.
θυμόν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (μελέων ἐξείλετο θυμόν ’took the life out of the limbs’)

θῖνα: θίς — shore, beach; fem. acc. sg.
θῦε: θύω (B) — rush, surge, rage; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔθυε); distinct from θύω ’sacrifice’
κάλλιμα: κάλλιμος — beautiful, fine (poetic by-form of καλός); adj., neut. acc. pl.

κέρδιον: κερδίων — more profitable, better; neut. nom. sg., comparative of κέρδος
καθῖζον: καθίζω — sit down, take one’s seat; impf. 3 pl.
κακὰ: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κακὰ ἔργα ’bad deeds’

καλέων: καλέω — call, summon, invite; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’calling’
καλλίτριχας: καλλίθριξ — fair-maned, fair-haired (καλός + θρίξ); masc./fem. acc. pl.

κείνου: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. gen. sg.
κεῖθι: κεῖθι — there; adv., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖ)
κλύον: κλύω — hear, hearken; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’they heard’
κλῦτέ: κλύω — hear, listen; aor. imper. 2 pl., + gen.: ’hear me!’
κούρης: κούρη — girl, maiden, daughter (Attic κόρη); fem. gen. sg.
κρατέρ: κρατερός — mighty, strong, harsh; neut. acc. pl., elided (κρατέρ’ = κρατερά)
κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
κῆρι: κῆρ — heart; neut. dat. sg., in the fixed adverbial idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περί used adverbially)
λίπ: λίπα — richly, thickly; adv. (perh. instead an elided case-form of a noun ’fat’, cf. λίπος), elided (λίπ’ = λίπα) · also λείπω — leave; aor. imper. 2 sg., elided (λίπ’ = λίπε): ’leave (me)’

μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.

μήλων: μῆλον — sheep, small cattle; neut. gen. pl.
μαντεύσομαι: μαντεύομαι — prophesy, divine (from μάντις); fut. 1 sg.
μεγάθυμον: μεγάθυμος — great-hearted, high-spirited; masc. acc. sg.
μεγάροις: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. pl.: ‘in the halls’
μεθήσει: μεθίημι — let go, relax, release; fut. 3 sg.
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μευ: ἐγώ — I; encl. gen. sg., epic μευ (= Attic μου): ’of me’, with κλύω ’hear me’ · also gen. with ἄγχι: ’near me’ (μευ ἄγχι στᾶσα) · also gen. of possession, ’my’ (οἵ μευ … κῆρ ’my heart’)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’)
μοῖραν: μοῖρα — due share, what is fitting, portion, fate; fem. acc. sg. (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μᾶλλον: μάλα — very, much; comparative adv. μᾶλλον: ’more, rather, the more’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
ναίων: ναίω — dwell, inhabit; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’dwelling’
ναιετάων: ναιετάω — dwell, live; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
νεστορίδη: Νεστορίδης — son of Nestor (patronymic, of Peisistratus); masc. voc. sg.
νεστορίδης: Νεστορίδης — son of Nestor (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
νηλῆα: Νηλεύς — Neleus; masc. acc. sg., epic -ῆα (= Attic -έα)
νηλῆος: Νηλεύς — Neleus, father of Nestor; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
νηῒ: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. sg., epic νηΐ (diaeresis marks the two syllables)
νοστήσει: νοστέω — return home; fut. 3 sg. act.: ’will return’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg., elided (νοστήσει’ = νοστήσειε), in an indirect question after a past verb: ’how he might return’ (ὅππως νοστήσει’ …)
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νύκτ: νύξ — night; fem. acc. sg., accusative of duration, elided (νύκτ’ = νύκτα): ’for the night’
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
ξείνια: ξείνιος (Attic ξένιος) — of or for a guest; τὰ ξείνια as noun, gifts and entertainment due to a guest; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ξεῖνοι: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); nom. pl.

οἴκαδε: οἶκος — house, home; + directional suffix -δε: ’homeward, to one’s home’
οἴκοι: οἴκοι — at home; adv. (locative of οἶκος)
οἶδα: οἶδα — know; perf. with pres. sense, 1 sg.: ’I know’
οἷο: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic οὗ): ’her own’
οἷος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg. · rough-breathed οἷος is relative ’such as, of the kind that’ (οἷος Ὀδυσσεὺς ἔσκεν ’such as Odysseus was’)
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὕτω: οὕτω(ς) — thus, so, in this way; adv.
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάντεσσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic πᾶσι)
πάρα: παρά — beside; πάρα (accent drawn back) stands for πάρεστι/πάρεισι ’is/are at hand, present’ · also prep. placed after its noun (anastrophe) · also adv. after its verb (anastrophe): ἐτίθει πάρα ’set beside’ (= παρετίθει)
πάσχων: πάσχω — suffer, experience; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’suffering’

παντοίην: παντοῖος — of every kind, all sorts of; fem. acc. sg.

ποικίλ: ποικίλος — inlaid, intricately worked; neut. acc. pl., elided (ποικίλ’ = ποικίλα)
πολλοῖσιν: πολύς — much, many; masc./neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic πολλοῖς): ’for many’
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
ποτὶ: πρός — to, toward, against; prep., epic ποτί, here as preverb in tmesis (ποτὶ … βάλε = προσέβαλε) · also a plain preposition + acc., no tmesis: ποτὶ τοῖχον ’against the wall’ · also + dat. ‘against’ · also + dat., ’on, upon’: ποτὶ χθονί ’on the ground’
πρήσσωμεν: πράσσω — do, accomplish, make one’s way; pres. subj. 1 pl., epic πρήσσω (= Attic πράσσω), + gen. of the way: ’that we may get on’
προθύροιο: πρόθυρον — forecourt, gateway before the house-door; neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
προσεφώνεε: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., augmented (προσ- + ἐ-φώνεε): ’was speaking to, addressed’
προσηύδα: προσαυδάω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg.
πρυμνῇ: πρύμνη — stern (of a ship); dat. sg.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf. · also + aor. subj., ’before’ (πρὶν … ἐπέλθῃ ’before it comes upon’) · also + opt.: ’before’ (πρὶν τλαίη ’before he would bring himself’) · also adv. with a finite verb, ’before that, sooner’ (πρὶν … ἀγείρετο ’before that … came gathering’) · also + fut. indic.: ’before’ (πρὶν … γαῖα καθέξει ’before the earth covers’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’
πτερόεντα: πτερόεις — winged (πτερόν ’feather, wing’); neut. acc. pl.: ’winged (words)’
πτολίεθρον: πτολίεθρον — citadel, city; neut. acc. sg., epic lengthened by-form of πόλις
πτόλιος: πτόλις (epic for πόλις) — city; fem. gen. sg. (= Attic πόλεως)
πυλίων: Πύλιος — Pylian, of Pylos; masc. gen. pl.
πόλλ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl., elided (πόλλ’ = πολλά): ’many’ · also used adverbially: ‘much, often’ (πόλλ’ ἐπέεσσιν ‘again and again with words’)
πόσις: πόσις — husband, spouse; masc. nom. sg. (distinct from πόσις ’drink’) · also πόσις — drink; fem. nom. sg. (βρῶσίς τε πόσις τε ’food and drink’)
πύλον: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; acc. sg.
πύλου: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; gen. sg.
πύλῳ: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese; fem. dat. sg.
πὰρ: παρά (apocope πάρ, functioning as an adverb) — beside, alongside; adv. · also a preposition + acc., ’beside’ (πὰρ Νέστορα) · also preverb in tmesis (πὰρ … θῆκεν = παρέθηκε ’set before’) · also a preposition + dat., ’beside’ (πὰρ πυρί ’beside the fire’) · also a preposition + gen., ’from (the side of)’ (πὰρ Ταφίων ’from the Taphians’)
πᾶσαι: πᾶς — all, every; fem. nom. pl.
πᾶσι: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl.
σεῖον: σείω — shake; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented: ’they shook’
σκιόωντό: σκιάω (also σκιόω) — cast a shadow, grow dark; impf. mid. 3 pl., epic diectasis (= Attic ἐσκιοῦντο)
σπουδῇ: σπουδή — haste, effort, zeal; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ‘with effort, barely’
συμφράσσατο: συμφράζομαι — plan together with, contrive jointly (+ dat. of person, + acc. of the plan); aor. mid. 3 sg.
σχεδόθεν: σχεδόθεν — from near, close at hand; adv., with the directional suffix -θεν
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)
τέκε: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔτεκε)
τήν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg., resumptive: ’whom’ · also demonstrative, fem. acc. sg., resuming an earlier noun: ’her’ (τήν … ῥέξω ’her I will sacrifice’) · also relative, fem. acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὀιζυῖ πολλῇ, τήν μοι ἐπῶρσε ’great misery, which he roused for me’) · also demonstrative with a noun and adjective: ’that’ (τήν γε στυγερὴν ὁδόν ’that hateful journey’)
τίσεται: τίνυμαι — take vengeance, punish; fut. 3 sg. mid. (τίσεται): ’will exact payment’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τελέεσθαι: τελέω — bring to pass, accomplish, fulfil; fut. inf. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic τελεῖσθαι)
τελέσειεν: τελέω — bring to pass, accomplish, fulfil; aor. opt. 3 sg. (wish): ’may he bring to pass’ · also potential (with κεν): ’might bring to pass’
τελεσφόρον: τελεσφόρος — bringing to completion, full (of a year’s cycle); masc. acc. sg.
τεύχε: τεῦχος — armour, gear (pl. τεύχεα); neut. acc. pl., elided (τεύχε’ = τεύχεα)
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τηλεμάχου: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. gen. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῖς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: masc./neut. dat. pl. ’in which, with which’ (τετυγμένα, τοῖς ἐνάμελγεν ’well-made, in which he milked’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. dat. pl.: ’the’ (ἰχθύσι τοῖς ὀλίγοισι ’for the little fishes’)
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’) · also demonstrative gen. of comparison after a comparative: τοῦ γε κρεῖσσον ’better than this’ · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐκ τοῦ: ’from that time’ · also neut. gen. sg., partitive, ’of it’ (τοῦ μὲν ὅσον τ’ ὄργυιαν ’of it, about a fathom’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the’ (τοῦ παιδὸς ’that son’) · also article-like gen. sg. with a noun and a participle (gen. absolute), distributive: ’of the one … of the other’ (τοῦ μὲν φθίνοντος μηνός, τοῦ δ’ ἱσταμένοιο ’as one month wanes and the other begins’)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; neut. nom. pl. (μῆλα, τὰ … κατάκειτ’ ’the flocks, which lie’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’, object of the verb in its clause (ῥωγαλέα, τὰ … ὅρηαι ’torn, which you see’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’) · also ’the other’, contrasted with a preceding τὴν … μέν: fem. acc. sg. (τὴν δέ ’the other one’) · also article-like with a numeral: ’the one’ (τὴν μὲν ἴαν ’the one portion’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον · also nom. dual with a noun, article-like: ’the two’ (τὼ … θεράποντε)
τῆος: τῆος — meanwhile, for so long; adv., epic (= Attic τέως), correlative of ἧος
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’)
υἱέος: υἱός — son; masc. gen. sg. (υἱέος Ὀρτιλόχοιο ’son of Ortilochus’, in apposition to Diocles)
φάνη: φαίνω — show; aor. pass. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐφάνη): ’appeared’
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φίλει: φιλέω — love, treat as a friend, entertain; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐφίλει)
φεύγων: φεύγω — flee; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
φημι: φημί — say, declare, assert; pres. 1 sg.
φηρὰς: Φηραί — Pherae, a town on the road from Pylos to Lacedaemon; fem. acc. pl.
φιλέειν: φιλέω — love, be fond of; pres. inf., uncontracted (= Attic φιλεῖν)
φιλότητος: φιλότης — friendship, love; fem. gen. sg.
φρένα: φρήν — mind, wits, heart; acc. sg. · also acc. of respect: ’in heart’ (γέγηθε φρένα ’is glad in heart’)
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φρονέοντι: φρονέω — think, consider; pres. part. dat. sg. masc., agreeing with οἱ: ’to him as he considered’ · also agreeing with ἐμοί: ’to me as I thought’ (ἐμοὶ πυκινὰ φρονέοντι)
φυλάκης: Φυλάκη — Phylace, a Thessalian town; fem. gen. sg., with ἐκ
φυτεύει: φυτεύω — plant, beget; pres. 3 sg., fig. ’set in motion (a disaster)’
φωνήσας: φωνέω — utter, raise one’s voice; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having raised his voice’
χρήματα: χρῆμα — thing, possession; (pl.) property, goods; neut. nom./acc. pl.
χρεὼ: χρεώ — need, necessity; fem. nom. sg. (indeclinable), impersonal with γίγνεται: ’a need arises’ · also with ἐστιν + gen.: ’there is need (of)’ (οὐ χρεὼ πείσματός ἐστιν ’there is no need of a cable’)
χρυσόθρονος: χρυσόθρονος — golden-throned; adj., fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses (an old alternative derives the second element from θρόνα ’embroidered flowers’)
ἀέκοντα: ἄκων — unwilling; masc. acc. sg., epic ἀέκων (= Attic ἄκοντα): ’against his will’
ἀγυιαί: ἀγυιά — street, road (in a city); fem. nom. pl.
ἀεικὲς: ἀεικής — unseemly, shameful, unfitting; adj., neut. acc. sg.
ἀθάνατοι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. nom. pl.: ’the immortals’
ἀθανάτοισι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀλφειὸς: Ἀλφειός — Alpheus, a river-god, father of Ortilochus; masc. nom. sg.
ἀμφὶς: ἀμφίς — apart, on both sides, around; adverb
ἀνά: ἀνά — up, up along; prep. + acc., or adv. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’mounted’); acute kept before an enclitic
ἀντίθεον: ἀντίθεος — godlike, a match for a god; masc. acc. sg.
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀργαλέῳ: ἀργαλέος — hard, grievous, painful; masc. dat. sg.
ἀργείοισιν: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Achaeans/Greeks; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀφίκετο: ἀφικνέομαι — arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.
ἀφνειὸς: ἀφνειός — wealthy, rich; masc. nom. sg.
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄεσαν: ἀέσαι (root ἀϝεσ-, prob. akin to ἰαύω ’sleep’; distinct from ἄημι ’blow’) — sleep, pass the night; aor. 3 pl.: ’they passed the night’
ἄλγεα: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive plain; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἄριστον: ἀγαθός — good; superl. ἄριστος, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’best’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with λαόν: ’best’ (λαὸν ἄριστον ’the best host’) · also masc. acc. sg. with the article, partitive: τὸν ἄριστον σιάλων ’the best of the hogs’
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἅρματα: ἅρμα — chariot; neut. nom./acc. pl. (pl. for a single chariot)
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκέλευσεν: κελεύω — command, order, bid; aor. 3 sg.
ἐλάαν: ἐλαύνω — drive; epic pres. inf. of the by-form ἐλάω, with diectasis (contracted ἐλᾶν; Attic pres. inf. ἐλαύνειν): ’to drive on’ · also, same spelling, fut. inf. (Attic ἐλᾶν): ’to be going to drive’, told apart only by context
ἐλθὼν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having come’
ἐμόν: ἐμός — my, mine; neut. voc. sg. (= nom./acc. in form; agrees with τέκνον) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: οἶκον ἐμόν ’my house’
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνιαυτὸν: ἐνιαυτός — year; masc. acc. sg., acc. of duration: ’for a year’
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπίθοντο: πείθω — persuade; mid. obey; aor. mid. 3 pl., augmented (unaugmented πίθοντο): ’they obeyed’
ἐπαληθεὶς: ἐπαλάομαι — wander about, roam over; aor. pass. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having wandered much’
ἐποτρύνων: ἐποτρύνω — urge on, spur on; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’)
ἐπῆλθε: ἐπέρχομαι — come upon, arrive; aor. 2 3 sg. (same form in Attic)
ἐρίγδουπος: ἐρίγδουπος — loud-crashing, traditionally loud-thundering (ἐρι- intensive; exact sense uncertain), epithet of Zeus; masc. nom. sg.
ἐριδούπου: ἐρίδουπος — loud-echoing, loud-thundering; masc./fem. gen. sg.
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθῆτα: ἐσθής — clothing, raiment; fem. acc. sg.
ἐτίσατο: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, take vengeance on; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’took vengeance (on)’
ἐφ: ἐπί (elided ἐφ’ before a rough breathing) — on, upon, over; + acc. · also + dat., with anastrophe (χερσὶ ἐφ’ ὕδωρ): ’over, upon (the hands)’ · also + dat. without anastrophe, ’over’ (ἐφ’ αἵματι φάσγανον ἴσχων ’holding the sword over the blood’) · also + acc., ’to, towards’, of destination (ἐφ’ ἡμέτερ’ ’to our (home)’)
ἑτάροισιν: ἕταρος — companion (by-form of ἑταῖρος); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἑταίρους: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. acc. pl.
ἑταῖροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form), address: ’companions!’
ἑῷ: ἑός (= ὅς, ἥ, ὅν possessive) — his own, her own; 3rd-pers. reflexive possessive adj., masc./neut. dat. sg., agreeing with θυμῷ: ’in his own (heart)’
ἔβαινον: βαίνω — go, step; impf. 3 pl. (or 1 sg.), augmented; in tmesis with ἀνά (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’they mounted’)
ἔκγονος: ἔκγονος — offspring, descendant; fem. nom. sg. (two-ending adj.), predicate: ’born of’
ἔκφυγε: ἐκφεύγω — flee out, escape; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐξέφυγε)
ἔλασαν: ἐλαύνω — drive; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented, in tmesis with ἐκ: ’drove out’
ἔλασεν: ἐλαύνω — drive, strike; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἤλασεν)
ἔμπης: ἔμπης — nevertheless, in any case, for all that; adv.
ἔναιε: ναίω — dwell, inhabit, live; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’was dwelling, lived’
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’) · also doubled, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’this way and that’
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with anastrophe, accent thrown back after its noun (δήμῳ ἔνι = ἐν δήμῳ) · also = ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι (ἔνι with no case): ’there is, there are in it/among them’ (ἄνδρες νηῶν ἔνι τέκτονες ’men, shipwrights, are among them’)
ἔξοχα: ἔξοχος — outstanding, preeminent; neut. pl. used as adv.: ’above all, outstandingly’
ἔπεα: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἔπη)
ἔπειθ: ἔπειτα — then, thereafter; adv., elided (ἔπειθ’ = ἔπειτα before a rough breathing)
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’) · also neut. nom. sg., in apposition/predicative, naming a maker: ἔργον Ἡφαίστοιο ’the work of Hephaestus’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a passive verb: ’work’ (τόδε ἔργον ἀέξεται ’this work grows’)
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔχοντες: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἠριγένεια: ἠριγένεια — early-born; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἠὼς: Ἠώς — Dawn; fem. nom. sg. · also a common noun, ’morning’ (ὄφρα μὲν ἠὼς ἦν ’as long as it was morning’)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤλασε: ἐλαύνω — drive, strike; aor. 3 sg.: ’drove, struck’
ἤλυθεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; epic aor. 3 sg. (= Attic ἦλθεν): ’came’
ἥδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., fem. nom. sg.
ἥρης: Ἥρη — Hera, wife of Zeus; fem. gen. sg., Ionic (= Attic Ἥρας)
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦμος: ἦμος — when, at the time when; temporal conj.
ἱέμενος: ἵημι — send, let go; mid. press forward, be eager; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἱκέσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; aor. inf.
ἵκανε: ἱκάνω — come to, reach; impf. 3 sg.: ’came upon’
ἵκετο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.; where the metre makes the ι long, that is the augment, which the spelling cannot show; with short ι, unaugmented
ἵκοντο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 pl.; with short ι (by metre) unaugmented; where the metre makes the ι long, augmented (the spelling cannot show it)
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα) · also relative adverb of place, ’where’ (= Attic οὗ): τῶν ἐνὶ δήμῳ, ἵν’ οἴχεται ’among those of the land where he has gone’
ἵνα: ἵνα — so that, in order that; + subj. · also + opt. after a past tense · also relative ’where’ + indic.: ἵνα … καθεύδετον ’where the two are sleeping’
ἵστατο: ἵστημι — set, stand; impf. 3 sg. mid./intrans. (neut. pl. subject with sg. verb): ’were standing’ · also with ἀνά in tmesis, masc. sg. subject: ’stood up, rose’ (ἀνὰ … ἵστατο)
ὀΐω: ὀΐομαι — think, suppose; pres. 1 sg. (act. form ὀΐω, epic; = Attic οἴομαι): ’I think’
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀρτιλόχοιο: Ὀρτίλοχος — Ortilochus, father of Diocles; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’)
ὁδοῖο: ὁδός — road, way, journey; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὁδὸς: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. nom. sg.
ὃν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (masc. acc. sg.)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄνομ: ὄνομα — name; neut. nom. sg., elided (ὄνομ’ = ὄνομα), subject of λίπηται: ’his name’
ὄχ: ὄχα — by far, exceedingly; adv., elided (ὄχ’ = ὄχα), intensifying a superlative (ὄχ’ ἄριστα ’far the best’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this (here); demonstrative pron., masc. nom. sg.
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅππως: ὅπως — how, in what way; epic ὅππως (double π metri gratia), with κε + subj. (or fut.): ’how you are to…’ · also + opt. in an indirect question after a past verb: ’how he might’ (ὅππως νοστήσει’ … ’how he might return’)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὦκα: ὦκα — quickly, swiftly; adv., from ὠκύς
ὧδε: ὧδε — here, to this place, in this way; adv.
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc. dat. sg.: ’his own (son)’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which; masc. dat. sg. (δοίη δ’ ᾧ κ’ ἐθέλοι ’give her to whom he wished’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg. (same form), agreeing with a neut. noun: πεδίοιο ... ᾧ ἔνι ... ’a plain in which is...’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg., agreeing with ἄχεϊ: ’her own (grief)’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥοδοδάκτυλος: ῥοδοδάκτυλος — rose-fingered; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
